explanation: A museum curator, Marjorie Courtenay-Latimer, spotted the strange blue fish in a fisherman's catch. Its fleshy, lobed fins mark it as a lobe-finned fish, the group that gave rise to land vertebrates.

claims.text: Before a living coelacanth was found off South Africa, the species was known from fossils and believed to have died out around the end of the age of dinosaurs.
Lungfish, sturgeon and hagfish were never thought to be extinct.
Museum curator Marjorie Courtenay-Latimer spotted the coelacanth in a fishing trawler's catch.
Coelacanths are lobe-finned fish, the group from which land vertebrates evolved.

evidence.restatement: Coelacanths were known only from fossils and thought to have died out at the end of the Cretaceous until a living one was caught off South Africa in 1938.

claimResults.note: Strictly, the group was known from fossils; the living species, Latimeria chalumnae, has no fossil record. The stem's 'Which fish' reads at group level, so the stem is accurate.

evidence.restatement: Lungfish, sturgeon and hagfish have always been known as living fish.
Marjorie Courtenay-Latimer of the East London museum spotted the fish in a trawler's catch in December 1938.
Coelacanths are lobe-finned fish (Sarcopterygii), the group from which land vertebrates evolved.

issues.note: The explanation's 'the group that gave rise to land animals' is broader than c4: lobe-finned fish gave rise to land vertebrates, not to insects or snails. 'land vertebrates' would be exact.

evidence.restatement: Coelacanths were known from fossils and believed extinct since the end of the age of dinosaurs until a living one was found off South Africa in 1938.

claimResults.note: Claim text says "the species"; strictly the coelacanth group was known from fossils, not the living species. Read as the group.

evidence.restatement: Lungfish, sturgeon and hagfish were never thought to be extinct.
Museum curator Marjorie Courtenay-Latimer spotted the coelacanth in a trawler's catch.

issues.note: Claim c1 says "the species" was known from fossils. Strictly, coelacanths as a group were known from fossils and the living species was unknown until 1938. The stem says "Which fish", so the player-facing text is fine; reword the claim if it is ever touched.
